name: HAPPY SMILE KOMEKO (ハッピースマイルこめこ)

claims.text: Shop is a 100% rice-flour (米粉) bakery and bakes no wheat products, so there is no wheat flour on the premises to cross-contaminate.
No published celiac cross-contact protocol; a new micro-bakery that also holds rice-flour baking classes.

Sweet/savory bagels use mochi, cheese, bacon, anko, chocolate and nut mix-ins; no soy-sauce-based items reported, but confirm the みたらし (mitarashi) glaze on 焦がしみたらし×チーズ, which traditionally contains soy sauce.
Several bagels contain dairy (cheese, white chocolate) and meat (bacon); no separate vegan production line noted.
No documented allergy-handling statement beyond the blanket gluten-free / additive-free claim; owner-operated, so ask directly.
Entire shop is gluten-free by design — 国産米粉100%・無添加 with no wheat baked on site.
The owner has independently researched and developed vegan, vegetarian, and allergen-conscious dishes, indicating awareness of dietary needs (no documented formal protocol).
All menus are prepared without fish, meat, dairy, or wheat, using carefully selected grains and vegetables with minimal additives and pesticides.
The kitchen describes its food as additive- and gluten-free (添加物・グルテン不使用), built around organic sprouted brown rice and house-made brown-rice noodles.
The signature tofu hamburger plate is explicitly noted as suitable for people practicing veganism.
「すべての商品がグルテンフリー」— all products are gluten-free and no wheat flour is baked on the premises, making wheat cross-contact inherently very low.
Some baked goods use oats/oatmeal alongside rice flour; oats are naturally GF but are a common cross-contamination vector unless certified, so highly sensitive celiacs should confirm sourcing.
Entire shop is vegan (no eggs, dairy or white sugar), so no animal cross-contact risk.
No published explicit celiac cross-contamination or allergen-handling protocol beyond the whole-shop gluten-free / plant-based positioning.
100% gluten-free, wheat-free and vegan product range — no wheat flour used in the shop at all.
Made without eggs, dairy and refined sugar; rice flour and koji based.

name: Chiffon no Mise PUKKU (シフォンのお店 PUKKU)

claims.text: Rice-flour-only chiffon specialist — no wheat flour is baked on premises, so flour-borne cross-contact is inherently low, but no formal celiac CC protocol is published.
Primarily a sweets shop; the café lunch (まんPUKKUランチ) may involve savory seasonings — confirm any soy sauce used is wheat-free (tamari) for celiac lunch guests.
Not applicable — products contain egg, milk and cream; no vegan line advertised.
The 100年しふぉん is explicitly promoted as 米粉100%のグルテンフリー made to give reassurance to customers, but individual allergen handling for café dishes is not documented online.
Whole chiffon range is 米粉100% / グルテンフリー with no wheat baking on site.
Signature cake uses traditional Nara 吉野本葛 and 米飴 instead of refined/wheat-based ingredients.

name: さくらパン工房 (Sakura Pan Kobo)

claims.text: This is a wheat-flour bakery using 100% domestic wheat for its main lineup; a gluten-free rice-flour bread is offered but no separate workspace, equipment or cross-contamination controls are documented, so cross-contact with wheat is likely.
Signature breads contain butter, eggs and dairy and are baked alongside all other products; no vegan-segregated handling is described.
All breads are made with natural fermentation and without synthetic additives such as emulsifiers, yeast food or dough improvers, using 100% domestic Hokkaido wheat.
A gluten-free rice-flour bread is available for customers who are concerned about gluten.

Small home-style kitchen with no documented dedicated gluten-free preparation or allergen separation; even though no wheat flour is used in the curries, fermented and seasoning ingredients may still introduce gluten or cross-contact, so coeliacs should ask about each day's specific dishes.

Curries are built on dashi and the rotating menu features chicken, seafood and egg, so vegan diners cannot assume shared pots or stocks are plant-based — confirm the bean curry and its dashi before ordering.

The kitchen explicitly does not use wheat flour or chemical seasonings, relying instead on dashi, salt, fermentation and spices — a meaningful starting point for gluten-sensitive diners (though not a verified celiac-safe environment).

name: しかさんしょこら（Shika san chocolat） (Shika san chocolat)

claims.text: The signature gateau au chocolat is made with no wheat flour and no rice flour, so the core product is naturally gluten-free by recipe.
A local news feature independently confirms the cake is made without wheat or rice flour and is naturally gluten-free.

name: 素味 スイーツ&コーヒー (Somi sweets&coffee) (Somi sweets & coffee)

claims.text: Not a dedicated gluten-free facility: wheat (ancient spelt) is used for the popular rum-raisin sandwich sable, so rice-flour items are baked in a kitchen that also handles wheat. Celiac visitors should ask which items are rice-flour-based and weigh cross-contact risk.
Entire shop is plant-based, so there is no animal-product cross-contact concern; all sweets and the coffee program are vegan.
All sweets are vegan and made with organic, transparently-sourced ingredients; many items are gluten-free rice-flour-based, giving plant-based and gluten-avoiding visitors plenty of reliable choices.
